title: Lie algebra is tangent space at identity
statement: For a field k and group scheme G over Spec k, after the canonical identity residue-field identification, the Lie algebra Lie G is k-linearly equivalent to the dual-number tangent space of G at the identity.

source.place: The infinitesimal-point identification in the identity tangent-space paragraph

proof.text: Use lieEquiv and infPointsEquivTangentGroup to identify the Lie algebra with dual-number group points reducing to the identity. Use the residue rationality of the identity to transport the dual-number source from k to the residue field. The two defining conditions are then exactly those of schemeTangentSpace. The inverse transports back.

The unit laws identify the differential of multiplication at the identity with the sum of the two tangent vectors; lieEquiv_mul gives additivity. Epsilon scaling and toLie_infPointsScale give compatibility with scalars, using Scheme.ΓSpecIso. These operations are the specified operations of schemeTangentSpace, so the bijection is a k-linear equivalence.

theorem exists_lie_identity_tangent_linearEquiv
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] :
    let x := unitSection G (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k)
    let r : k →+* G.left.residueField x :=
      (StructureSheaf.toStalk k (G.hom x) ≫ G.hom.stalkMap x ≫ G.left.residue x).hom
    letI : Module k (schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom x) :=
      Module.compHom (schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom x) r
    Nonempty (Lie G ≃ₗ[k] schemeTangentSpace k G.left G.hom x)
